description: Issue #839 AC2, the cross-kind collision in the STRUCT-FIRST direction: `struct tally [ x y ]` then `define tally`. Its mirror (`define` then `struct`) is `struct-reserved-word-procedure`; both must report `ol-duplicate-definition` naming the FIRST declaration, which is what proves the runtime keeps ONE first-declaration map across both declaration kinds rather than one map per kind. With separate maps this direction would report nothing at all, because the `define` would be the procedure map's first entry — the defect the checker's own equivalent had before issue #838's review. `spec/error-model.md:126` covers exactly this case: "a procedure and a struct with the same name in either order".

diagnostics.message: you already defined tally on line 1.
